headline: NEW -- Gunmen attack Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, Karak (Jordan) during funeral
dek: Two gunmen (footage shows three firing from street) stormed the Hamoud Greek Orthodox church compound in Karak during a funeral procession, firing continuously ~5 minutes on 150-200 mourners. PSD first reported 7 dead, later revised to 6 killed and 28 wounded (27 in hospital).
sources: Jordan Public Security Directorate statement (Maj Gen Abdallah al-Maaytah presser); state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka (security-camera footage, Reuters-verified); King Abdullah II (X post + hospital visit)
fault_line: Homegrown extremism vs a regional proxy trying to fracture Jordan — commenters split between mourning/unity and blame arguments (one reel 12K likes/830 comments; another 20K likes).

sections.what_happened: Two gunmen (footage shows three firing from street) stormed the Hamoud Greek Orthodox church compound in Karak during a funeral procession, firing continuously ~5 minutes on 150-200 mourners. PSD first reported 7 dead, later revised to 6 killed and 28 wounded (27 in hospital). No claim of responsibility; interior minister called it a 'group of extremists' but said links to known groups are not established. King Abdullah condemned it as a terrorist attack and promised retaliation 'with an iron fist'; manhunt ongoing. Rare attack on Christians in the kingdom.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (JPost/CNN/WSJ chains), CNN, WSJ, Al Jazeera, The National, Straits Times, Vatican News, WION, Gulf News, Siasat; Al-Mamlaka security footage verified by Reuters
sections.what_disputed: Death toll revised 7->6 during the day; no perpetrator identity or motive established — any attribution (ISIS precedent 2016 Karak, Iranian targeting this year) is speculation at this hour. Authorities have not released suspect names or group links.
sections.why_matters: Jordan — the kingdom Washington calls one of its most reliable partners, used as a basing point in the Iran war — hit at a funeral in a Christian village. The King promises the harshest retaliation; the manhunt is still open and nobody has claimed it. On screen: verified facts only, the toll revision, and the one question nobody can answer yet — who wanted to break Jordan.
